body L32-L35: Nallino's addenda et emendanda (Part I, p. LXXII) add to pp. 162-163 that Theon's strange definitions are found also in the unpublished Astrologia of Vettius Valens, book II, in the chapter on the winds of the stars (περὶ ἀνέμων τῶν ἀστέρων): after Salmasius (De annis climactericis, pp. 421-422), Valens puts with the other astrologers the exaltation of the Sun in 19° of Aries, takes the square with its vertices in 19° of Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn, and says that the Sun descends the north from Aries to Cancer, descends the south from Cancer to Libra, ascends the south from Libra to Capricorn and ascends the north from Capricorn to Aries, and the like of the other planets; of the Moon, whose exaltation is in 3° of Taurus, book I (Salmasius, p. 422) says the same with the square Taurus, Leo, Scorpius, Aquarius. Julianus of Laodicea (the passage cited on p. LXXI) agrees with al-Battānī's usage: the Sun, Venus and Mercury, at the longitudes 214° 8′ 50″, 231° 28′ and 224° 32′, descend to the south (κατέρχεται νότον), the Moon and Saturn, at 48° 10′ and 24° 28′, ascend to the north (ἀνέρχεται βοῤῥᾶν); Nallino takes the same words said of Jupiter (154° 12′) and Mars (137° 35′) for a corruption of the copyists.
